statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 4, low, because CME equity index futures have been halted since Friday at 21:00Z and this final pre-reopen slot contains no tradable Nasdaq-100 interval at all; the twenty-three slots from the 22:00Z scheduled reopen onward carry conditional Tail readings between 10 and 18, every one of them below the block threshold. Stress is 45, elevated, one point above the previous hour and at the top of its pre-reopen arc, with roughly half an hour left before the venue reopens and the weekend queue still unpriced: a US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions confirmed for 18:00Z Monday, a long end whose 30-year closed near 5.273% on Friday, a semiconductor complex down about 5% on the week, and Nvidia results plus the Jackson Hole symposium later in the week. None of it can be priced until the venue reopens. Confidence is 84, high, on index levels confirmed directly at the index owner, H.15 yields, settled oil and volatility prints and a verified calendar, held below very-high only because no live Nasdaq-100 price path exists inside a weekend halt.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path: the Nasdaq-100 traded a 29,142.44 to 29,405.12 range on Friday and settled at 29,308.86, up 0.33% on the day but roughly 2% lower on the week, while the VIX finished at 14.89 after a 14.77 to 15.95 range. Both session extremes were retraced, so no persistent directional efficiency is on record and nothing in the current evidence set establishes one. The material change this hour is horizon rather than news: the published window now reaches through the late Monday US session, so the 18:00Z Treasury news conference, the hour that follows it and the final cash hour are all carried. Tail-relevant structure cannot be observed again until the 22:00Z reopen, roughly half an hour away, so the narrow evidence-based danger window continues to cover 22:00Z to 02:00Z, when the weekend information set is repriced into thin liquidity. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Final closed hour before the 22:00Z reopen: Tail holds the floor of 4 with no tradable interval in the slot, then carries conditional readings between 10 and 18 from the reopen through Monday's full US session, with the 18:00Z Treasury sanctions news conference, the hour after it and the late cash hour all inside the window.
body: CME Globex equity index futures stopped trading for the week on Friday at 21:00Z and are scheduled to reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, roughly half an hour after this assessment. The twenty-four slots published here run from 2026-08-23T21:00:00Z to 2026-08-24T20:00:00Z, so one closed hour is followed by the reopen slot and twenty-two tradable hours. Monday's 12:30Z Chicago Fed release, the 13:30Z US cash open, the 15:30Z bill auctions, the 18:00Z US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions, the 19:00Z hour that follows it and the 20:00Z late cash hour all fall inside the horizon. The Nasdaq-100 settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 95.69 points or 0.33%, having traded a 29,142.44 to 29,405.12 range; the level, high, low and net change are confirmed directly at the index owner, and a widely used quote page again served an inconsistent level this hour and was resolved against the index owner rather than carried forward. Both Friday extremes were retraced, which is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that would justify a raised Tail. On the week the Nasdaq Composite fell about 2% and the S&P 500 about 1.4% as long-end yields pressured growth, with the Philadelphia semiconductor index down about 5%; the 10-year closed near 4.734% and the 30-year near 5.273% on Friday, against H.15 observations for 20 August of 2-year 4.19%, 10-year 4.69% and 30-year 5.23%. WTI settled at 87.06 dollars after a second consecutive weekly gain above 5%, a cross-asset pattern consistent with geopolitical and fiscal risk premia rather than with an equity liquidation, and the VIX at 14.89 after a 6% daily decline does not corroborate index stress. Delayed shared cross-asset context for the last session shows Nasdaq futures firmer by 0.30%, the VIX future 1.68% lower, gold 2.39% higher, Treasury futures lower across the curve with the 30-year contract weakest, five of eight megacaps positive with wide dispersion, and semiconductors mildly negative at three of seven higher; it is used only as confirmation or conflict and never as live price-path evidence. That semiconductor and megacap split is a conflicting rather than an aligned backdrop, which under the applied framework reduces directional conviction instead of raising Tail. No new verified market-moving item has been published since the previous hour; Monday's news conference, Nvidia results on 26 August and the Jackson Hole symposium from 27 August remain scheduled catalysts carried in the event calendar, not reported outcomes. Tail stays at 4 for the remaining shut hour because no Nasdaq-100 price path can form inside it.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: 19 hourly assessments are available and 5 clock-hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable (21:00Z on 22 August, then 07:00Z, 10:00Z, 11:00Z and 12:00Z on 23 August). Across every available hour Tail held 4 and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON, so no hour approached the block threshold and the dominant mode remained normal throughout. Stress traced a shut-weekend arc, easing from 40 at the start of the window to a low of 34 through the European morning before turning higher across the afternoon and evening to 44 in the most recent published hour as the reopen drew closer. Confidence eased from 87 to 84 as the last observed session receded further into the past.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this final pre-reopen slot, while Stress tops its pre-reopen arc at 45. The remaining twenty-three slots are tradable. The 22:00Z scheduled reopen and the first full hour after it carry a conditional Tail of 15 on the untested assumption that a weekend gap could extend before retracing; an orderly two-way reopen would invalidate that. Conditional Tail then decays to 10 through the quiet Asian hours, where two-way trade has historically been most reliable, before rebuilding through the European session to 14 into the 12:30Z Chicago Fed release, 16 at the 13:30Z US cash open and 17 in the first full cash hour, easing across the auction block and midday lull to 14, then reaching the window maximum of 18 in the 18:00Z slot containing the scheduled US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions and holding 18 in the 19:00Z slot where a delayed second leg would sit, before easing to 16 in the final published cash hour. Every one of the twenty-four published slots stays below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON across the whole window. None of the post-reopen structure is observed; each figure is a conditional reading that a genuine two-way path would reduce and that shallow pullbacks with repeated extension would raise.
